title: Reconstruct the VAE
summary: Move from approximate posterior parameters through differentiable sampling to the reconstruction-plus-KL objective.

parts.title: Why a distributional encoder?
parts.prompt: What does q(z|x) provide that a deterministic autoencoder bottleneck does not?
parts.answer: It represents uncertainty and regularizes nearby inputs into a structured latent distribution. Sampling from the prior can therefore produce meaningful decoded examples.
hints: A deterministic code has no explicit prior match.

parts.title: The reparameterization trick
parts.prompt: Why write z=mu+sigma*eps instead of sampling z directly from q(z|x)?
parts.answer: Moving randomness into an independent epsilon makes z a differentiable deterministic function of mu and sigma. Gradients can then flow through the sampled latent into encoder parameters.
hints: Differentiate z with respect to mu and log variance.

parts.title: Balance the ELBO
parts.prompt: What roles do reconstruction error and KL divergence play in VAE training?
parts.answer: Reconstruction preserves information needed to explain x. KL keeps each approximate posterior near the prior, making the latent space sampleable and preventing isolated codes.
hints: One term preserves data; one shapes latent geometry.
Too much KL can cause posterior collapse.

parts.title: Implement reparameterization
parts.prompt: Transform mu, log variance, and fixed epsilon into a differentiable latent sample.

parts.title: Implement the VAE loss
parts.prompt: Return mean squared reconstruction loss plus mean KL divergence to a unit Gaussian.
